implement.approach: rateLimit.ts: auth-failure budget split into two aligned windows sharing AUTH_FAILURE_LIMIT (30/300s). Egress window (scope 'authfail', id=IP) now counts DISTINCT refused credentials per window — charged only when a credential's per-(IP, sha256(credential) prefix) shard (scope 'authfail_id') records its FIRST failure (atomic INCR ordinal == 1, never read-then-write) — plus credential-less refusals (no bearer: nothing a peer could share, charged per hit as before). Shard window bounds one client's replay to AUTH_FAILURE_LIMIT on its own. Pre-auth gate peekAuthFailureBudget() peeks egress then shard, reporting the closed window's Retry-After. 401s are tagged via a WeakMap<Response, AuthRefusal> (authRefusal/authRefusalOf): kind 'liveness' (session fenced at this edge after logout — cached revoked entry or verification racing revocation — or Supabase Auth 403 session-gone) charges only the shard, never the egress; kind 'credential' (bad/expired/forged bearer, refused refresh token — identity = hash of the refresh token, deletion-status capability as bearer) charges shard + egress-on-first. Unavailable Auth (429/5xx/network) still 503s uncharged (unchanged). Regression test rateLimit_nat_budget.test.ts drives the real handler through routesHarness with fetch interception for Auth verdicts; 4 scenarios: replayed refused bearer isolated to its shard while a peer stays signed in; rotating refused bearers still trip egress (stuffing protection kept); liveness 401s (edge-fenced after logout and upstream 403) bounded per shard and never charged to egress; replayed refused refresh token charges egress once while peers keep refreshing.
out_of_scope_files: supabase/functions/api/index.ts — edge-index serial group IS held by this package (manifest serial_groups: ["edge-index"]). Minimal wiring only: import list, the pre-auth gate peeks the sharded budget for the presented bearer (peekAuthFailureBudget), recordAuthFailure charges via chargeAuthFailure with the refusing Response, the four 401 charge sites pass their response, and the five refusal sites in authenticate()/refreshSessionRoute() tag their 401 with authRefusal(); no existing code moved or reformatted, no existing comments modified.
residual_risks: Egress budget semantics changed from 'every refusal' to 'distinct refused credentials + credential-less refusals': a single client rotating forged bearers still trips it in 30 attempts, but 30 replays of ONE dead credential no longer close the egress (by design, per objective). Documented in rateLimit.ts doc comments.

Shard keys add up to one extra rate-limit window per distinct refused credential per IP; memory fallback capacity (MEMORY_WINDOW_MAX = 20 000 live windows) is shared with all other budgets — an attacker rotating many credentials from one IP is still bounded by the egress window (30) before it can consume meaningful capacity.

Liveness classification relies on Supabase Auth returning 403 for a revoked/gone session (existing verdict mapping in authenticate()); a 401 from Auth for a still-signed but revoked token is charged as a credential refusal (conservative: never under-charges an attacker).

implement.approach: Test-first: rateLimit_nat_budget.test.ts written against the real index.ts handler (routesHarness loadHarness/loadIsolate) and proven to fail on BASE (11/14). Then rateLimit.ts gained an auth-failure budget model — AuthFailureKind credential|liveness|expired, authFailureIdentity (sha256 prefix of the presented credential, opaque), authRefusal/authRefusalOf (WeakMap tag on the 401 Response), authRefusalKind (GoTrue error_code → kind), peekAuthFailureShard, peekAuthFailureBudget (egress + shard), chargeAuthFailure. Accounting: every refusal INCRs the per-egress+credential shard (authfail_id); only the first credential refusal of a distinct credential INCRs the egress-wide budget (authfail, via authfail_cred ordinal); liveness INCRs only the shard; expired returns before any charge; a per-egress open-shard tally (authfail_shards) caps shard creation at 2×limit — past it a credential refusal charges the egress directly and liveness charges nothing, so an unauthenticated caller cannot mint 20 000 keys. All writes are the existing atomic INCR paths (Redis or memory). index.ts got the minimal wiring: AuthVerdict.refused carries error_code; local expiry tagged expired; fenced sessions tagged liveness; GoTrue refusals classified by error_code (403 bad_jwt = credential, 403 session_not_found = liveness); refresh route shards by refresh-token identity; dispatcher peeks egress+shard and charges by tagged kind.
out_of_scope_files: supabase/functions/api/index.ts — minimal additive wiring hunk (serial group edge-index, not held by this package): import the new rateLimit.ts exports, carry GoTrue error_code on AuthVerdict.refused, tag the existing 401 sites with their refusal kind (authRefusal), and swap the pre-auth peek/charge calls for peekAuthFailureBudget/chargeAuthFailure; without it the objective is an unused module. No existing code moved or reformatted; existing comments untouched.

residual_risks: Shard-cap check is a read (authfail_shards) before the atomic shard INCR, so a concurrent burst of N distinct new credentials on one egress can open up to N shards past AUTH_FAILURE_SHARD_CAP (=2×limit=60) before the cap engages; it never under-counts the egress or double-charges a replay, and the isolate table remains bounded by MEMORY_WINDOW_MAX. Tested for correctness, not for that transient overshoot.

Every authenticated request now does two rate-limit reads pre-auth (egress budget + presented credential shard) instead of one; with Upstash configured that is one extra REST GET per request on the hot path (memory fallback: negligible). Not benchmarked (UNKNOWN latency delta).

Liveness classification is by GoTrue error_code allow-list (session_not_found, session_expired, user_not_found, user_banned); any other 401/403 (including bad_jwt and an absent error_code) is a credential failure — safe direction (charges), but a future GoTrue code for a session-state refusal would be charged as credential until added.

An attacker who rotates >60 distinct forged credentials per 5-min window per egress hits the shard cap and is then charged straight to the egress budget (same as BASE); peers behind that egress are locked out for the window exactly as on BASE — the package objective isolates replays, expired bearers and liveness, not an active >30-distinct-credential stuffing run (which the egress budget is FOR).
Redis path (Upstash) exercised only through the memory-fallback isolate and the recorded-callback harness; no live Upstash run (UNKNOWN).
implement.summary: Defect on BASE d8e5db3e (VERIFIED by the new test file failing 11/14 there): supabase/functions/api/index.ts keyed the auth-failure budget by IP only — `peekRateLimit('authfail', ip, 30, 300)` pre-auth and `recordAuthFailure()` → `enforceRateLimit('authfail', ip, …)` on every 401 (bad bearer, refused refresh, refused ID token, and the local `bearerExpired` short-circuit at index.ts ~1010-1015 which never contacts Auth) — so 30 refusals of ONE replayed bearer, or 30 handsets waking with their own expired bearer behind one NAT/venue egress, returned 429 to every valid bearer, bootstrap and refresh from that address (the old xc_adjudication_auth.test.ts:667 characterization pinned exactly that lockout). `authRequest()` discarded GoTrue's `error_code`, so 403 bad_jwt (credential) and 403 session_not_found (liveness) were indistinguishable; rateLimit.ts had no notion of identity or refusal kind.
